title: October 2026: the frameworks say Neutral
summary: 28 frameworks, one stance: Neutral, with a score of +0.36.

sections.heading: The short version
paragraphs: The consensus for October 2026 is Neutral. That means holding your neutral mix. The frameworks do not agree strongly enough to lean either way.
The score is +0.36 on a scale from -1 to +1. It takes +0.5 or more to lean into stocks and -0.5 or less to lean away. The driver families contributed +0.50. The alarm families took 0.14 off.

sections.heading: What changed since last month
bullets: Growth and inflation quadrants moved from Positive to Neutral.
High-yield spread regime moved from Clear to Watch.
Seasonality and election cycle moved from Negative to Positive.
Market breadth moved from Negative to Positive.
Dow Theory moved from Neutral to Positive.
Multi-asset trend moved from Positive to Neutral.

sections.heading: Where the frameworks agree and disagree
paragraphs: Of the 25 frameworks that feed the score, 14 are positive or clear, 6 are neutral or on watch, and 5 are negative.
The negatives: Don't fight the Fed, Buffett indicator, Shiller CAPE and excess CAPE yield, Fed model (equity risk premium) and Rule of 20.
bullets: Macro regime (+0.33): Stagflation: growth slowing, inflation accelerating; Overheat: growth above trend, inflation rising; Mid cycle.
Policy and liquidity (0.00): Fed is hiking; Policy is 0.9 pts looser than the rule; NFCI -0.46 (looser than average); Net liquidity +0.6% over 6 months.

Trend and momentum (+1.00): S&P 500 is 3.8% above its 10-month average; Golden cross: 50-day above 200-day; Stocks +10.8% over 12 months vs 4.0% in T-bills; Holds Foreign stocks; 64% of sectors are above their 10-month average; Industrials and transports both in uptrends.
Sentiment and calendar (+0.50): November 2026: inside the November to April window, post-midterm window; Bulls minus bears: -4 points.
Recession risk (0.00): 13% recession probability; Sahm reading 0.00; CFNAI 3-month average +0.02; Claims -14% from a year ago.
Credit and volatility (-0.29): High-yield spread 3.44%; VIX one-month average 16.9.

Valuation (-1.00): Stocks are 255% of GDP, 100th percentile of history; CAPE about 40.0 (estimated), 98th percentile of history; Stocks yield 1.0 pts less than the 10-year Treasury; P/E plus inflation is 27.8.
Where to look (not scored): In uptrends: US stocks, Commodities; Leading: Energy, Health care, Technology. Lagging: Consumer discretionary, Utilities, Communication; 1 of 3 growth ratios are rising.

sections.heading: What this means for a portfolio
paragraphs: For a neutral mix of 60% stocks, 30% bonds, 5% cash, 5% alternatives, the rules give 60% stocks, 15% bonds, 15% cash, 10% alternatives this month.
Counting each framework's own playbook: 5 favor stocks, 2 favor bonds, 4 favor cash and 3 favor alternatives.
Valuation reads expensive, so even an Overweight would be half the usual size.
bullets: Stocks stay at neutral because the consensus is Neutral.
Alternatives get 5 extra points: inflation is accelerating.
The Fed is hiking, so half of the bond-and-cash sleeve sits in cash and T-bills.

sections.heading: Framework in focus: Shiller CAPE and excess CAPE yield
paragraphs: Compare the market's price with ten years of inflation-adjusted earnings so that one boom or bust year does not distort the ratio.
This month it reads negative: CAPE about 40.0 (estimated), 98th percentile of history.
Where it has failed: It has been above its long-run average for almost all of the past 30 years. Accounting changes and buybacks make old and new readings hard to compare.

sections.heading: What would change the picture
paragraphs: The score would need to rise 0.14 to reach Overweight or fall 0.86 to reach Underweight, and hold there for two months.
Alarms on watch: High-yield spread regime. A move to triggered would pull the score down.

disclaimer: This brief is assembled from the model's rules. It describes what well-known frameworks say about current conditions. It is not a forecast and it is not personal investment advice.
